title: Exclusive | Quantum Startup Oratomic Now Worth $5.4 Billion After Series-B Funding
key_facts: Oratomic raised $475 million in Series B at a $5.4 billion valuation
Financing announced 8 Oct 2026; amount and valuation disclosed by law firm Wilson Sonsini
Total funding $775 million since public launch in March; $300 million Series A in July
Co-leads: ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Bezos Expeditions
Builds quantum computers from neutral-atom arrays held by laser beams
CEO Dolev Bluvstein; founders tied to Caltech (Endres, Preskill, Huang)
March Caltech-Oratomic proposal: useful machine with 10,000-20,000 qubits instead of millions, theoretical only
No timetable for a working system; mission is utility-scale machines by end of decade
quote_evidence: Local quantum computing startup Oratomic has raised $475 million in Series B financing, pushing its valuation to $5.4 billion, according to the law firm that represented the company in the transaction.
That finding is theoretical, not evidence that such a computer has been built.
Its October announcement did not establish a timetable for completing a working system.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows investor appetite for neutral-atom quantum computing despite no built machine yet.
notes: WSJ article paywalled (401); read Pasadena Now. Underlying financing dates from 8 Oct 2026, so older news re-dated by the WSJ exclusive; score lowered by 2. WSJ headline not read in full.
